correctness.rationale: Disjoint checks give a Cartesian product of one-block hulls. Every admissible sign vector remains exposed as a cube vertex. For m_j≥3, fixing one or two signs leaves respectively 2^(m_j−2) or 2^(m_j−3) completions, so the vertex mean is zero and covariance is I_N. Averaging enclosing ellipsoid inequalities gives tr(A^(−1))+z^T A^(−1)z≤1, yielding det(A)≥N^N with equality only for the centered ball. A negative sign product requires at least one reversal and the cheapest costs exactly 2M_j. Gaussian sign parity is fair and independent of magnitudes, and radial independence divides the expected Gaussian support width by E R=a_N. This gives the stated width and, because p_(r−1)−2p_r+p_(r+1) is the integral of q^(r−1)(1−q)²>0, the two strict extremal partition rules (trivial for k=1). Opposite directions flip the sign product precisely in odd blocks, establishing the exact loss and its zero atom. For the minimum limit, independently obtained the global dominance q(t)≤exp(−ct): if f(t)=c exp(−t²/2), then q(t)/f(t)=integral_0^infinity exp(−tu−u²/2)du≤1/c. Thus q(s/m)^m≤exp(−cs), justifying all fixed moments by dominated convergence as the tails tend to exp(−cs). The per-block limiting odd/even variances are respectively 4/c² and 12/c²; uniformly bounded third moments give Lyapunov's CLT when k,m both grow. The uncentered sum of scaled block losses is O_P(k); dividing the radial normalization error by sqrt(k) costs O_P(sqrt(k/N))=o_P(1), with no need for independence of that error. The fixed-k laws follow by joint independent block convergence and Slutsky. Finally 2kp_m/a_N is asymptotic to sqrt(2 pi) k²/N^(3/2). The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its integer directions and finite quadrature are supplementary.
residual_risks: The stated fluctuation limits and crossover assume equal blocks with m→infinity, and the CLT also requires k→infinity. No analogous limit for heterogeneous sizes or overlapping checks was verified.

evidence: The one-block correction, opposite-direction parity effects and one-block laws are known or closely overlapping ingredients. The classical body and group do not distinguish different product block profiles with the same N and k.
Strict curvature of the half-normal-minimum tail integral, and control of radial fluctuation when the number of blocks grows, supply the additional extremal and fluctuation conclusions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Support additivity, half-normal minima and standard CLT tools are not themselves new. The checked findings do not determine the unique two extremal profiles or the two parity CLTs and the crossover for the specified joint limit. Those are the supported distinct claims, rather than the isolated single-block formulas or enclosing balls.

originality.rationale: The demihypercube, even-check formulation, support optimization, reflection symmetries and related single-block enclosing ellipsoid facts are not credited as new. The supported distinction is exact strict balancing and maximal imbalance of intrinsic widths for product block profiles, together with the parity-dependent multi-block fluctuation and scaling laws. The closest indexed type-B/type-D width result has substantial one-block overlap, but its stated class and conclusions do not cover these product and growing-block assertions; it is also dated later than the frozen record.
residual_risks: The original single-spin-ellipsoid catalogue comparison 15c85fee505a and the synchronized-parity full text were not located. No novelty credit is assigned for the one-block ellipsoid.
The finite search cannot exclude an earlier equivalent width/fluctuation result under coding-theory or product demihypercube terminology.

value.rationale: The exact volume-free-width comparison shows that Euclidean mean width distinguishes independent-check arrangements not distinguished by vertex count, vertex radius, covariance, or the enclosing ball. It gives both optimizing profiles and a concrete k versus N scale on which the deficit stays observable, and explains why parity shows up in width fluctuations despite identical first-order block means. The intrinsic comparison is useful on its stated family without claiming a general coding-theoretic theorem.
residual_risks: The crossover concerns absolute, unscaled mean-width deficit; no nonzero relative-width loss or applicability to overlapping constraints is inferred.
